newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Jordan envoy cancels resignation.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Jordan envoy cancels resignation.

text.p: Israel's ambassador to Jordan said on Tuesday he was withdrawing his resignation a week after announcing he was quitting in protest at being kept in the dark over a secret meeting between the leaders of the two countries.

"The conditions have been created that enable me to agree to (Foreign Minister David Levy's) request that I return to my post," ambassador Oded Eran told Israel Army Radio, declining to go into details.
Eran quit a week ago after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a secret meeting in Jordan with King Hussein over a water dispute without informing the envoy or the Israeli embassy in Amman.

"There is a need to brief the embassy on actions being taken," Israel Radio quoted Eran as saying in a sharply worded letter of resignation last week after news of the meeting appeared in an Israeli newspaper.

In the Army Radio interview, Eran sidestepped questions about the reasons for quitting but said he hoped his short-lived resignation would lead to "improved relations" between the Prime Minister's office and the Foreign Ministry.
Eran, formerly deputy director general for economic affairs at the Foreign Ministry, is Israel's second ambassador to Jordan since embassies were opened in the wake of a 1994 peace treaty.
